task: Implement dedicated workforce login plus canonical TOTP enrollment and challenge UX on top of the existing workforce assurance primitives without enabling global AAL2 authorization enforcement.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This UX handles privileged workforce sign-in state, TOTP enrollment secrets and AAL2 challenge transitions. It must consume the canonical workforce assurance policy and Supabase MFA authority without creating browser persistence or silently turning this UX block into global authorization enforcement.

acceptanceCriteria: A dedicated workforce sign-in route accepts staff/platform credentials and preserves a safe originally requested admin or preview destination.
When the canonical policy requires MFA and no verified TOTP factor exists, the UI starts TOTP enrollment and shows both QR setup data and the manual secret fallback.
When a verified factor exists but the current session is below AAL2, the UI challenges an existing verified TOTP factor and refreshes the assurance state after successful verification.
A platform owner is guided through enrollment until two verified TOTP factors exist; one verified factor is never presented as owner-ready.

Enrollment cancellation and provider failures leave the user on the workforce auth surface with an explicit recoverable state and do not persist OTP secrets in localStorage, sessionStorage or application storage.
Successful workforce authentication returns to the safe requested workforce destination while ordinary shopper/customer authentication remains on the existing customer flow.
The surface remains usable on narrow mobile and desktop layouts without introducing a separate MFA or OTP authority.
invariants: Supabase Auth remains the only MFA factor, TOTP secret and challenge verification authority.
The existing workforce assurance policy remains the only Shoperation authority for required factor counts and next MFA step.
Customer sign-in and customer MFA policy are not changed by workforce-intent routing.
This block does not add requireAdmin or middleware AAL2 authorization enforcement.
Only verified TOTP factors count toward policy readiness; abandoned unverified enrollment never counts.
Return targets are same-origin relative workforce destinations and cannot become open redirects.

failureModes: A platform owner signs in, verifies one TOTP and is sent to the requested admin page before the second verified factor exists.
An MFA provider/listFactors/AAL load error is mistaken for a zero-factor or ready state and bypasses enrollment or challenge.
The enrollment QR secret is copied into browser persistence and becomes a second long-lived application secret store.
An attacker supplies an absolute or protocol-relative next target and turns workforce login completion into an open redirect.
The customer account route starts enforcing workforce MFA merely because an admin-intent adapter was added.
A cancelled unverified enrollment remains orphaned and later confuses factor selection or verified-factor counting.
edgeCases: Platform owner with zero verified factors must enroll factor one, verify it, then enroll and verify factor two before completion.
Platform owner with one verified factor at AAL2 must still enroll a second factor rather than being considered complete.
Platform owner with two verified factors at AAL1 must challenge an existing verified factor before completion.
Merchant owner/admin with one verified factor at AAL1 challenges rather than re-enrolling.
Low-risk support/viewer workforce with zero required factors completes first-factor login without being globally MFA-blocked.
A workforce login request without a safe next target falls back to the canonical admin landing page.
Cancelling an in-progress unverified enrollment attempts cleanup but never removes an already verified factor.

alternatives.summary: Add a dedicated workforce route that consumes the existing assurance policy and MFA client primitives, while keeping shopper auth separate.
alternatives.reason: This creates the requested staff/admin UX without duplicating authentication policy or changing customer authentication semantics.

alternatives.summary: Add staff role detection and MFA enrollment directly inside the existing shopper AuthForm.
alternatives.reason: It would mix customer and workforce concerns, increase authority ambiguity and risk accidental customer MFA policy changes.

alternatives.summary: Enforce AAL2 immediately in middleware and requireAdmin while building the UI at the same time.
alternatives.reason: The Product Owner explicitly separates UX proof from the later high-risk enforcement block; combining them would expand blast radius and obscure failure diagnosis.

specialistReviews.finding: The workforce UX must be a consumer of canonical identity policy rather than a route-local MFA policy engine.
specialistReviews.resolution: The client obtains workforce role context from a server route, then uses requiredWorkforceTotpFactors/nextWorkforceMfaStep and the existing workforce MFA client primitives.

specialistReviews.finding: Displaying enrollment secrets and handling redirects introduces secret-leak and open-redirect risk; cancellation can also leave unverified factors behind.
specialistReviews.resolution: Enrollment material stays in React memory only, return targets are restricted to relative workforce routes, and cancellation only unenrolls the current unverified enrollment factor.

specialistReviews.finding: Reusing the customer auth surface or inventing route-specific factor rules would repeat second-authority and navigation-drift failure classes.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use a dedicated workforce surface plus a narrow fiokom workforce-intent adapter; do not change ordinary customer sign-in behavior.

challenge.scenario: A platform owner signs in with zero factors and successfully verifies the first enrollment.
challenge.finding: If completion is evaluated immediately after AAL2 promotion, one factor could incorrectly finish the owner flow.
challenge.resolution: Reload the MFA snapshot after verification and re-run canonical next-step policy; owner remains in enrollment until two verified factors exist.

challenge.scenario: A user already has a verified factor but the current session is only AAL1.
challenge.finding: Starting another enrollment would create unnecessary factors and not prove possession of the existing second factor.
challenge.resolution: Select an existing verified TOTP factor and run challengeAndVerify, then reload the snapshot.

challenge.scenario: The server cannot resolve a workforce role/context after first-factor sign-in.
challenge.finding: Treating the actor as low-risk would turn missing authorization context into an MFA bypass.
challenge.resolution: The workforce context endpoint fails closed; the UI signs no authorization claim and does not continue to the requested destination.

challenge.scenario: The user cancels while a new TOTP enrollment is unverified.
challenge.finding: Leaving the factor behind can create orphaned MFA setup state and repeated confusing enrollments.
challenge.resolution: Track only the current enrollment factor in component memory and attempt unenroll on cancel before returning to the sign-in-ready state.

challenge.scenario: A crafted next query contains //evil.example or an unrelated customer route.
challenge.finding: Blind navigation after MFA would create an open redirect or cross-surface flow confusion.
challenge.resolution: Normalize only same-origin relative workforce targets and fall back to /admin.

challenge.scenario: A low-risk staff member without an MFA requirement signs in through the workforce route.
challenge.finding: A blanket MFA screen would violate the accepted policy and create unnecessary workforce lockout.
challenge.resolution: The server returns canonical role context and the shared policy can return zero required factors, allowing completion without enrollment.

challenge.scenario: MFA snapshot or challenge verification throws midway through the UI flow.
challenge.finding: A success redirect from stale client state would convert provider failure into fail-open behavior.
challenge.resolution: All MFA transitions are awaited, errors remain on the auth surface, and navigation occurs only after a fresh snapshot reports ready.

proofPlan: Run deterministic workforce auth UX regression tests covering safe return targets, workforce/customer separation, owner two-factor sequencing, challenge flow, enrollment cancellation and forbidden browser persistence.
Run the existing workforce identity primitive regression suite to prove the UX still consumes the canonical policy and Supabase MFA authority.
Run exact-head TypeScript validation and production build to prove the new App Router route, server context handler and client MFA surface compile together.
Verify the final diff does not add AAL2 enforcement to middleware, requireAdmin authorization decisions or customer MFA policy.
Use exact-head CI evidence for Truth Gate and close the lifecycle only when every completion requirement and forbidden regression is VERIFIED.

requirements.requirement: A dedicated workforce login flow authenticates staff/platform users and returns successful sessions only to a safe originally requested workforce destination.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Workforce login must not accept protocol-relative, absolute or non-workforce return targets.
Ordinary customer login must not be globally replaced or MFA-mandated by this workforce route.

requirements.requirement: The workforce auth surface supports TOTP QR/secret enrollment, verified-factor challenge and platform-owner two-factor sequencing through the existing canonical MFA primitives.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The UX must not create custom OTP verification or persist TOTP secrets in localStorage, sessionStorage or application storage.
A platform owner with only one verified TOTP factor must not be treated as complete.

requirements.requirement: The MFA UX handles provider errors and cancelled enrollment while remaining responsive, and it does not enable the later global AAL2 authorization-enforcement block.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: This block must not add global AAL2 enforcement to middleware or active admin authorization decisions.
MFA provider or snapshot failures must not trigger a success redirect.

notes: Stage 1 MR1-WORKFORCE-IDENTITY UX block only. Existing canonical assurance/TOTP primitives are consumed, not reimplemented. Global admin AAL2 enforcement remains explicitly deferred.
